dup2(input_pipe[0],STDIN_FILENO) intentionally establishes child standard input for exec. Only the pid==0 branch duplicates descriptors; original pipe ends and inherited descriptors >=3 are closed, while stdin/stdout/stderr survive exec by design. Any duplication/exec failure calls _exit, whose process teardown closes all descriptors. No parent descriptor is created by child dup2. The raw GCC16 trace reports a leak at the duplication itself, before these lifetime/exec transitions.

dup2(output_pipe[1],STDOUT_FILENO) intentionally establishes child standard output across exec, not a retained parent FD. executor.c:326-344 duplicates only after fork in pid==0, closes all original pipe ends and inherited descriptors >=3, then execs or _exits; failure and eventual child exit close standard descriptors. GCC16 reports a leak at the deliberate duplication before modeling process/exec ownership.

dup2(error_pipe[1],STDERR_FILENO) intentionally establishes child stderr across exec. executor.c:326-344 closes original pipe ends/inherited descriptors >=3 and execs or calls _exit; descriptor 2 belongs to that child until its exit. The parent never executes dup2. The raw GCC16 creation-site leak diagnostic omits this intentional standard-stream process lifetime.
